summary: The code is syntactically valid and has many components for an agent-based mask adoption simulation, but it is incomplete and non-executable. Core simulation methods (Simulation.step, run, visualize, save_results, validate) are missing. Additionally, the required direct main() call is mistakenly placed inside a docstring, so it will never execute. As a result, the implementation and logic do not meet the specified task requirements.

issues.description: Simulation.run is called in main() but not implemented. This will raise an AttributeError when executed.
issues.location: class Simulation (missing run method); referenced in main()
issues.solution: Implement Simulation.run(self, days: int) to initialize state (if not already), loop over days calling self.step(day), update series/metrics, and return results.

issues.description: Simulation.step is declared but has no body; it only contains a docstring. The simulation's daily logic is missing.
issues.location: Simulation.step definition at the end of the file
issues.solution: Provide a full body for step() to update risk perception, adoption decisions, information broadcast, policy enforcement, social influence, purchases, movement/contacts, observational learning, and metrics recording.

issues.description: Visualization, result saving, and validation methods are invoked but not implemented: visualize(), save_results(), validate().
issues.location: class Simulation (missing methods); referenced in main()
issues.solution: Implement visualize(self) (optionally using matplotlib), save_results(self, path) (e.g., write series to CSV), and validate(self, num_runs, days) (e.g., run multiple times, summarize metrics).

issues.description: The direct call to main() is placed inside a triple-quoted docstring of Simulation.step, so it will never execute. This also violates the requirement to call main() at global scope.
issues.location: Within the docstring of Simulation.step: the lines '# Execute main...' and 'main()' are inside the docstring string
issues.solution: Close the step() docstring correctly, add the function body, and then place a direct call to main() at module scope after all definitions, not inside any string or guard.

issues.description: The code does not yet realize the specified interactions and metrics end-to-end: SocialInfluence, ObservationalLearning, PolicyBroadcastAndCompliance, PolicyEnforcementEncounter, InformationExposure, PurchaseMasks, MovementAndContact are only partially scaffolded. Metrics such as adoption_rate_over_time, context_specific_adoption, policy_compliance_rate, purchase_conversion_rate, and adoption_inequality are not computed.
issues.location: Simulation.step (missing), various classes; series fields defined but not populated
issues.solution: In step(), implement the daily pipeline: broadcast information, compute peer and observational signals per location, update beliefs and risk, decide adoption, attempt purchases via retailers/supply chain, simulate movements/contacts and enforcement, update compliance, record all required metrics (including context-specific adoption and inequality via Gini/variance).

issues.description: Epidemic context and policy thresholding are defined but not integrated into daily decision-making due to missing step/run implementation.
issues.solution: In step(), call epidemic.update_case_rate(day) and update_risk_signal(), use PolicyAuthority.issue_mandates(day, epidemic) to set mandates for locations, and feed public_risk_signal into risk perception; also call _simulate_infections(day) to evolve disease and close the perception loop.

issues.description: Retailer restocking and supply chain production are defined but not exercised daily.
issues.solution: During each step, call supply_chain.produce_masks(), then for each retailer call retailer.begin_day(), retailer.restock_from_supply(), handle customer purchase attempts via retailer.sell(), and adjust prices (retailer.update_price and supply_chain.adjust_prices).

issues.description: Scale-free network generation maintains a 'targets' list that grows with edges; for large N this is O(E) memory, which is acceptable for N≈5k but could be optimized.
issues.solution: Optionally switch to alias sampling or degree arrays to avoid duplicating nodes in 'targets', or use a network library (e.g., networkx) if allowed.

issues.description: The Vendor entity from the spec is represented as Retailer; there is no explicit InformationSource entity as described (though InformationChannel and MediaChannel cover similar roles).
issues.location: Entities: Retailer vs. Vendor; InformationChannel/MediaChannel vs. InformationSource
issues.solution: Either document the mapping (Retailer=Vendor, InformationChannel/MediaChannel=InformationSource) or add thin wrapper classes to match the spec names/attributes.

issues.description: Minimal error handling is present. main() wraps visualize() in try/except, but run(), save_results(), validate() (once implemented) should handle invalid parameters and IO errors.
issues.solution: Add input validation, bounds checks (e.g., for probabilities), and exception handling (e.g., IOError when saving CSV).

issues.description: Some imported modules are unused due to missing implementations (e.g., csv, sys).
issues.solution: Use these imports in the appropriate implemented methods or remove them to keep the code clean.
